_doc: Functional benchmark for GitLab #813. Each task is graded by RUNNING the generated program, not by parsing it. `grade_by` is 'execution_output' (the program must run and print the expected output, compared the way Tests/IntegrationTestsRunner compares an example against its expected.txt) or 'aro_test' (the generated application must pass the Given/When/Then file in `test`, which asserts values rather than printing). `reference` is a solution verified against the toolchain; `python3 Train/script/functional_eval.py --reference` re-verifies every one of them and is the guard against the benchmark rotting.

tasks.prompt: Write a complete ARO application whose Application-Start logs exactly `Hello, ARO.` to the console.
Write a complete ARO application that computes 7 * 6 and logs the result to the console, then returns OK.
Write a complete ARO application that uppercases the string "aro" and logs it to the console.
Write a complete ARO application that sums the list [10, 20, 30, 40] and logs the total to the console.
Write a complete ARO application that computes the average of [10, 20, 30] and logs it to the console.
Write a complete ARO application that logs each of the names Alice, Bob and Carol on its own line, in that order, using a for each loop.
Write a complete ARO application that creates a score of 80 and logs the word `pass` to the console only when the score is 50 or more.
Write a complete ARO application that reads the file ./sample.txt and logs how many lines it contains.
tasks.reference:
(Application-Start: Line Count) {
    Read the <content: raw> from "./sample.txt".
    Compute the <lines: lines> from <content>.
    Compute the <count: length> from <lines>.
    Log <count> to the <console>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <startup>.
}

tasks.prompt: Write a complete ARO application with a user-defined action called Double that takes a number and returns it doubled as the field `doubled`, and an Application-Start that calls it with 21 and logs the result.
Write a complete ARO application that removes duplicates from the list ["red", "blue", "red", "green"] and logs how many distinct values remain.
tasks.reference:
(Application-Start: Tags) {
    Create the <all-tags> with ["red", "blue", "red", "green"].
    Compute the <tags: unique> from <all-tags>.
    Compute the <count: length> from <tags>.
    Log <count> to the <console>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <startup>.
}

tasks.prompt: Write a complete ARO application that joins the list ["a", "b", "c"] into one string separated by ", " and logs it.

Write a complete ARO application with a list of people, each an object with name and age, and log the name of every person aged 18 or over, one per line. Use Alice aged 30, Bob aged 12 and Carol aged 18.

Write an ARO application with a feature set named `get-length` in the business activity `String Utils` that computes the length of a variable named `text` and returns it. Also include an Application-Start that returns OK.

Write an ARO application with a feature set named `cart-total` in the business activity `Cart` that sums a list variable named `prices` into a result named `total` and returns it. Include an Application-Start that returns OK.
Write a complete ARO application that stores two users in the user-repository and then logs how many users it holds.
tasks.reference:
(Application-Start: Users) {
    Store the <first> to the <user-repository> with { id: 1, name: "Alice" }.
    Store the <second> to the <user-repository> with { id: 2, name: "Bob" }.
    Retrieve the <users> from the <user-repository>.
    Compute the <count: length> from <users>.
    Log <count> to the <console>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <startup>.
}

tasks.prompt: Write a complete ARO application that emits an OrderPlaced event carrying an order, with a handler feature set that logs `order received` when the event arrives.
Write a complete ARO application that sorts the list [3, 1, 2] and logs each value on its own line, smallest first.

Write an ARO application with a feature set named `apply-discount` in the business activity `Pricing` that multiplies a variable named `price` by 0.9 and returns the result as `discounted`. Include an Application-Start that returns OK.
